I've been thinking a lot recently about the censorship that Google/Facebook and such have been engaging in of late and how it aligns with a libertarian perspective. It's led me to a couple questions that maybe someone here can answer.

Understanding that by and large the libertarian response to such censorship is that these are private companies and have the right to refuse their services to whomever they want, how far does this principle extend? There's a lot of things the government does today that libertarians of all stripes feel should be privatized. Roads, Fire, police etc... So, it would be illegal for the fire department to refuse to respond to a call of a fire at a black persons house. However, if the fire department were to be privatized, then they're free to do business with whoever they want? So a private fire department could discriminate all they want, as long as its not the government?

Or say private roads. Let's say I'm Zuckerberg rich... Could I buy up all the roads leading into and through a town and declare that no hispanics may enter or travel on my roads?

It seems to me that if you say that no, that's not appropriate and shouldn't be legal, it would be in conflict with allowing companies to remove sites of the internet and censor individuals.

If you say yes, while unfortunate it absolutely should be legal/allowed, then what's the difference between government oppression and corporate oppression, particularly if we move towards a more libertarian society where corporations are responsible for much of what the government currently does?

That's a good question. In similar cases of tension between private company rights and public interest, I tend to go with the principle of transparency and disclosure. That is, you can do anything that is legal but you are required to disclose it to your customers and users. E.g. if you censor right leaning videos creators, you need to disclose the criteria you use and the magnitude of that censorship.

Transparency and disclosure preserve one's rights on one hand and make sure the agreements between parties are really consensual, knowing all the facts and aspects.

I don't know if this is the kind of answer you are looking for but in my mind it's a reasonable balance between the two goals.

Thanks for responding. A follow up question; is it okay then, in your opinion, for the government to discriminate then as long as they disclose the fact that they will be discriminating? If not, why the difference between government and corporations?

Corporations are associations of private citizens pursuing their happiness. Your questions should then can be reduced to should the government be allowed to do everything that private citizenss can do. My answer to that is clearly no. Government has extreme monopolistic powers that call for extreme restraint and oversight (e.g. it can jail you, it can take your money forcibly as taxes, etc) and it has a constitution obligation to treat all citizens equally. Private citizens don't have those powers and constitutional obligations.

That's my 2c. I am sure that when analyzing the details we can find edge and gray cases but this is my general sentiment.

The more I think about it, the more it seems to me that the key aspect is the monopoly. Mostly, I'm fine with private parties being able to do whatever they want. I don't think anyone should be forced to "bake that cake" for example. If a baker tells you to fuck off, it's easy to go to another baker. However if the government or corporation tells you that you can't use a road, well there isn't an alternative.

My overall aim here is to find a principle that applies. I'm no Stormfront fan, but I don't think it's right they're being chased off the internet. That would seem to contradict my opinion on the bakers... I consider myself pretty libertarian so I thought this would be a good place to ask

The world is complex. You need to accept that at best your will find general principle, not exact rules that will be perfect in every imaginable scenario. ;-)

Or say private roads. Let's say I'm Zuckerberg rich... Could I buy up all the roads leading into and through a town and declare that no hispanics may enter or travel on my roads?

If you want to get a full libertarian perspective on this, I recommend you read this. I think roads should be more like public utilities, since they operate under natural monopolies. Each private road company gets a certain area for them to solely cover, like how no two cable companies can be in the same areas nowadays. It wouldn't be good for business if that road company forbid hispanics from using its roads, because you don't see water or electric utilities doing this, for the same reason: a profit motive and the fact that they have to provide for the entire public since the product or service they provide is under a natural monopoly.

When it comes to "undesirables", the problem is that this is a highly subjective area. Not to mention that it would be rather hard to prove when it comes to largely invisible things like drug use. And since we're talking about a hypothetical libertarian world, most things that are considered "undesirable" (drug use, incest etc.) would be legal and thus less stigmatized anyway (see drug use after legalization in Portugal).

 

But at the end of the day, my original thought holds true: unless your profit is lower when providing your goods/services to that group, it would make no sense to refuse them service, since not only would your future prospects be restricted, but it would be far easier for your competitors to run you out of business.
